title: Photos and voice notes
hook: Text-only, OCR, vision models, specialist models, speech. Pick by what the picture must tell you.

useCase.title: "My blender arrived broken", with a photo
useCase.story: Customers send photos and voice notes. The bot must judge the damage, read the label, and extract the serial number.

approaches.name: Ignore the photo
approaches.avoidWhen: The photo carries the key information.
approaches.example: The bot asks the customer to describe the damage.

approaches.name: OCR, then text
approaches.what: Read printed text out of the image, then treat it as normal text.
approaches.example: Read the serial number from the sticker.

approaches.name: Vision-capable language model
approaches.what: The model looks at the image directly.
approaches.greatWhen: Judging damage, scenes and mixed content.
approaches.avoidWhen: Precise measurements, or very blurry images.

approaches.name: Specialist vision model
approaches.what: A model trained for one visual job.
approaches.greatWhen: Millions of images, one narrow job, and speed.
approaches.example: A defect detector on a packing line.

approaches.name: Speech to text, then text
approaches.what: Transcribe the voice note, then process it like any message.
approaches.example: A voice note is transcribed and classified.

challenge.question: A customer sends a photo of a cracked blender jar. What is the best approach?

options.text: Ignore the photo and ask for a description
options.why: The photo already has the answer.

options.text: A vision model to judge the damage, OCR for the sticker, and a person for low-confidence cases
options.why: Each tool does the job it is best at, with a safety net.

options.text: Train a custom defect model from scratch
options.why: No data and no time for a first version.
Great for the sticker, blind to the crack.

bestCase.title: A vision model for judgement, OCR for exact text, a person for edge cases
bestCase.example: Photo in. The model says "glass jar visibly cracked at the base". OCR reads serial BL-2291 from the sticker and matches it to the order. The refund workflow starts, flagged for a quick human check.

worstCase.title: Trusting a blurry photo without a check
worstCase.example: A dark, blurry photo. The model confidently says "no damage" and the refund is denied. Or it reads serial BL-2291 as BL-2281, which belongs to a different customer's order.

route.travelling: A photo of a blender with a cracked jar

steps.label: Quality check
steps.goes: Is it sharp and bright enough to use?
steps.goesWrong: A blurry photo goes straight to the model.

steps.label: Vision model and OCR
steps.goes: One judges the damage. The other reads the serial sticker.

steps.label: Confidence gate
steps.goes: High confidence continues. Low confidence goes to a person.

steps.label: Refund workflow
steps.goes: It continues into the refund flow from the workflow stop.

takeaway: Match the tool to the job: OCR for exact text, a vision model for judgement, specialists for volume, and a person when confidence is low.
